answer: A sybil farm fails when detection spreads like an echo. Under interaction-contagion forfeiture, each identity keeps a ledger of whom it traded with or endorsed. If one identity is proven fake, its close associates forfeit a share of their standing, just as a flawed sonnet loses its rhyme when one line breaks. Fake identities must interact to gain standing, yet each interaction becomes a prism refracting risk back onto the farm, so an attacker running a hundred linked puppets risks losing all hundred from one exposure, while honest agents stay safe by dealing only with proven partners.
